finding.problem: The change lets an agent confirm elements, but several existing statements still say only a person confirms. The confirm_element description says 'Only a person confirms.' The glossary entry for element says 'confirmed only by a person.' The Element object description says 'confirmed by a person.' These now contradict the new action and were not updated.

findings.label: seeded
findings.why: It flags that the edit leaves 'Only a person confirms' statements contradicting the new agent-confirm action, which is the conflict with the only-a-person-confirms rule.

finding.problem: confirm_wording_fix passes approver = actor.id to the kernel's confirm_element, but the agent role has no world actor. The approver value is undefined or an agent id. The kernel's confirm_element, which until now only received a person's id as approver, may reject it or record a non-person as approver. The confirmation that fills the human-only slot is therefore not attributable to a person.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: The agent has no world actor so approver = actor.id is undefined or non-person, a real attribution problem but not the seeded rule conflict itself.

finding.problem: The wording_only flag is a free optional parameter set by whoever proposes the element, and the precondition only checks the flag. Nothing verifies that the change is wording only. A proposer can mark a substantive element wording_only and bypass the human-confirmation rule. The flag is also not reset or re-checked when record_proposal re-proposes an element.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: wording_only is a proposer-set flag that is not verified, so substantive elements can bypass human confirmation; a real loophole but not the seeded conflict.

finding.problem: The only new example is the denial case. No scenario shows the agent successfully confirming an element with wording_only true, and none shows that the agent cannot use confirm_element. The allowed path and the new human-requirement boundary are untested. The World fixtures also have no element with wording_only set.

findings.label: false-alarm
findings.why: Missing positive-path example and fixtures is a test coverage remark, not a real defect in the change's behaviour.

edit.why: It adds an agent role and a confirm_wording_fix action that confirms elements only when wording_only is true, with transitions, precondition and example, which does what was asked.
